subject.title: Memory MVP: define SQLite schema and canonical record model

question: Should memory-core move durable memory from Markdown files to a plugin-owned typed SQLite record model for the MVP, and what migration, provenance, review, and forget semantics must ship with it?
rationale: The request defines a persisted user-state model that affects memory ownership, migrations, review/forget flows, provenance, and several open Memory MVP sibling issues; automation should not choose that contract alone.

options.title: Approve plugin-owned SQLite MVP contract
options.body: Define the v1 schema/status/revision/provenance contract first, then implement it in memory-core with explicit migration and review boundaries.

options.title: Keep Markdown canonical for now
options.body: Continue treating SQLite as retrieval/index infrastructure around MEMORY.md and daily Markdown notes, then narrow or close this schema request later.

options.title: Defer until memory convergence
options.body: Keep this as design backlog until maintainers choose the recommended memory plugin path described in VISION.md.

recommendation.title: Approve plugin-owned SQLite MVP contract
recommendation.body: Define the v1 schema/status/revision/provenance contract first, then implement it in memory-core with explicit migration and review boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal on the current memory storage, memory-host SDK, and Markdown-plus-index model this request would replace or migrate.
